sections.content:
You know impersonal value judgements like *es importante que* and *es una lástima que* with the present subjunctive from A2 Unit 27. At C1, the same grammar carries sharper evaluative adjectives and shifts across time frames with the present perfect and imperfect subjunctive.

In debate and opinion columns, speakers replace neutral *es bueno* / *es malo* with precise judgements: *resulta absurdo que*, *es lamentable que*, *parece indignante que*, *es discutible que*, *fue desacertado que*. Even when the speaker knows the fact is real, the clause after *que* takes the **subjunctive** because the main clause evaluates it rather than asserting it (*Es lamentable que hayan pasado por alto ese detalle*).

Match the subjunctive tense to the time frame: use the **present subjunctive** for present/future situations, the **present perfect subjunctive** for a completed past action judged from today (*Resulta indignante que hayan subido la tarifa*), and the **imperfect subjunctive** after a past evaluation (*Era absurdo que pagaran tanto*). When there is no specific subject, keep the infinitive (*Es lamentable pasar por alto el mérito del equipo*).

sections.title: Evaluative subjunctive across time frames
rows: *Es discutible que el proyecto merezca tanto presupuesto.*
Present judgement + completed past -> present perfect subjunctive
*Es lamentable que hayan pasado por alto las quejas.*
Past judgement + past event -> imperfect subjunctive (*-ra / -se*)
*Parecía indignante que cobraran una tarifa tan alta.*
*Resulta desacertado ignorar el mérito del equipo.*

items.spanish: Resulta absurdo que nadie haya revisado las cifras antes de firmar.
items.english: It is absurd that nobody checked the figures before signing.

items.spanish: Es lamentable que pasen por alto el mérito de los técnicos locales.
items.english: It is regrettable that they overlook the credit of the local technicians.

items.spanish: Era indignante que el servicio dejara tanto que desear después de la reforma.
items.english: It was outrageous that the service left so much to be desired after the renovation.

items.spanish: Es discutible que esa medida sea la más acertada para el barrio.
items.english: It is debatable whether that measure is the wisest one for the neighbourhood.

sections.content: Do not switch to the indicative just because the event really happened: *Es lamentable que subieron la tarifa* is non-standard in careful Spanish; use *Es lamentable que hayan subido* (or *subieran/subiesen*). By contrast, expressions of plain fact (*Es verdad que*, *Está claro que*) keep the indicative.
